title: Executive Assistant to the Founders
description:
We are hiring an Executive Assistant to the Founders to own the calendars, correspondence, travel, and follow-through of our two co-founders.

Pairs is where founders come to raise capital. We pair them with the right investors from a large, engaged global investor network, then our agents manage the relationships that turn into meetings. It is a two-sided platform, live with paying clients, profitable and self-funded, built by a small, senior, flat team that ships fast.

The role

The two co-founders carry the work that decides this company: product, clients, the investor network, the brand. Their time is the scarcest resource in the business, and protecting it will be your mandate. You manage both calendars across time zones, own both inboxes, plan and oversee travel, prepare the founders for the meetings that matter, and ensure every commitment they make is kept. This is a position of ownership, not a list of tasks. You exercise judgment, act independently, and involve the founders only when a decision genuinely requires them. You work AI-first, like the rest of the company: tooling carries the mechanical work, and your time goes to judgment, anticipation, and trust. You report directly to both co-founders and hold one of the most trusted positions in the company.

What you will own

- Both calendars across time zones: scheduling, conflicts resolved before they surface, preparation time protected, and our Monday and Thursday meeting rhythm maintained.

- Both inboxes: triaged daily, replies drafted in each founder's voice, nothing important left waiting.

- Travel end to end: planned, booked, briefed, and resolved in real time when plans change.

- Meeting preparation and follow-through: the right briefing beforehand, actions captured and pursued afterward.

- The commitment layer: what the founders have promised, to whom, by when, tracked to completion.

- The systems behind it all, built on the best AI tooling, so mechanical work never requires attention twice.

You are a fit if you

- Have supported a founder or C-level executive at a fast-moving company, and can describe what never required their attention because of you.

- Have managed calendars across three or more time zones and understand the craft: buffers, batching, protected working time, and declining requests on someone else's behalf with grace.

- Write well enough to draft in another person's voice, and judge well enough to know what can be sent without asking.

- Have owned travel end to end, including disruptions resolved before the principal ever felt them.

- Can support two principals at once: competing priorities held, both agendas moving, neither founder resolving minor conflicts.

- Treat discretion as a reflex: names, transactions, and conversations remain confidential, always.

- Build systems rather than task lists: standing rhythms, documented processes, and automation that outlasts your busiest week.

- Operate with modern tooling: AI runs your scheduling, briefings, and follow-ups, so your time goes to judgment rather than administration.

What we offer

Fully remote. This position operates in real time across the founders' working day rather than asynchronously. Meetings across the company batch on Mondays and Thursdays, and you are the one who maintains that rhythm. The best AI tooling, paid (Claude Code, Cursor, top models). Direct trust from both co-founders, full visibility into the company, and a position that grows as the company does.

How to apply: hit apply, which takes you to our short application form. We read every application. Please do not include the names of former principals or any of their confidential matters; we evaluate how you work, not who you have worked for.

title: Software Engineer, AI accelerator Runtime
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

You will build the low-level device runtime that turns compiled programs into efficient, functional and performant execution on OpenAI’s custom AI accelerator. This software will schedule kernel launches, manage device memory and address spaces, coordinate synchronization, and expose reliable abstractions to higher-level runtimes and frameworks.

You will work at the boundary of software and hardware, partnering with compiler, kernel, architecture, verification, and silicon teams to define interfaces and validate behavior. You will also use and improve event-based, cycle-accurate simulation to develop runtime capabilities before silicon is available, diagnose performance and correctness issues, and guide hardware-software co-design.

In this role, you will:

- Design and implement the low-level device runtime for OpenAI custom silicon.

- Build kernel-launch scheduling, command submission, queueing, dependency tracking, and completion handling.

- Manage device memory spaces, allocation, virtual-to-physical mappings, data movement, and lifetime across concurrent workloads.

- Implement synchronization primitives, events, barriers, streams, and ordering guarantees that are correct and efficient.

- Define clean interfaces between the runtime, drivers, firmware, compiler-generated code, kernels, and higher-level execution systems.

- Use event-based, cycle-accurate simulators to develop, validate, debug, and performance-tune runtime behavior before and after silicon availability.

- Diagnose concurrency, memory-ordering, deadlock, race, correctness, and performance issues across software and hardware boundaries.

- Build tests, tracing, profiling, observability, and reproducible workloads for runtime correctness and performance.

- Partner with architecture and silicon teams to turn workload and simulator insights into hardware-software interface improvements.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have strong low-level systems programming experience in C, C++, Rust, or comparable environments.

- Have built runtimes, drivers, firmware, operating-system components, accelerator software, or adjacent systems infrastructure.

- Understand concurrency, synchronization, asynchronous execution, queues, events, and memory-ordering semantics.

- Understand memory management, address spaces, DMA, caching, coherency, and hardware-software interfaces.

- Have hands-on experience with event-based, cycle-accurate simulators or closely related architectural and performance models.

- Can reason quantitatively about scheduling, latency, throughput, utilization, contention, and resource tradeoffs.

- Are skilled at debugging failures that span software abstractions, device interfaces, and hardware behavior.

- Work effectively across compiler, kernel, architecture, verification, firmware, and silicon teams.

To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations.

description:
Senior Engineering & Integration Manager 

About the company: 

In the coming decades, our world needs substantially more critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and cobalt, to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. The mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago, because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.

KoBold is a leading scientific mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to make discoveries faster-by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. We made our first discovery-Mingomba, one of the world’s largest undeveloped high-grade copper deposits-after spending materially less than the industry average. This asset is expected to operate for decades, and be a leading global copper supplier. KoBold is actively running exploration programs in 8 countries worldwide, all with the potential for another high-quality discovery.

We are developing Mingomba by applying the same technical rigor to resource development and mine planning as we do to exploration. Mingomba is also a scientific laboratory where we prototype new technology and workflows, combined with the expertise of veteran engineers. Our multidisciplinary team consists of mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. We want to develop world-class mining projects that are safer and have more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. 

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

 

About the role

This is a senior Engineering leadership role for the development of a significant Copper mining complex in Zambia. The Mingomba deposit contains over 10 million tonnes of copper more than half of which exceeds 6% grade. This role will help turn that world class deposit into a world class mine.

The Senior Engineering & Integration Manager is the primary technical authority for the Mingomba copper project through its design and construction phase. Reporting to the Project Director, this role carries end-to-end accountability for the quality, integrity, and integration of all engineering across the owner's team, the EPCM and specialist contractors. The role is the technical decision-maker and design authority for the project, responsible for safeguarding Kobold’s interests through stage gates, design reviews, and construction handover to operations. The Senior Engineering & Integration Manager sets the direction for engineering delivery, resolves complex cross-discipline technical issues, and directly influences how the Mingomba project is designed and built.

 

What this role is accountable for delivering

This role exists to ensure against common failure modes on major capital projects, with particular emphasis on scope creep driven by unresolved technical decisions, design quality that does not survive construction, and an owner's team that cannot effectively challenge or govern its engineering service providers.

The successful candidate will be judged on:

• Engineering delivered on time, within sanction cost, and to the standard required for safe, operable, and maintainable facilities.

• A design that has been constructability-reviewed, value-engineered, and operability-tested before it is frozen.

• An EPCM that is technically directed, not just administered, with KoBold holding design authority.

• A project that passes independent technical assurance review

description:
Who we are
Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.
As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.
Why Spain
Some of our most mission-critical team members are based in Spain, having joined us from companies like Wise and Glovo. Moniepoint is one of the largest and fastest-growing digital banks in Africa, and this is an opportunity to work on genuinely impactful problems: disrupting financial services at scale in emerging markets, and building systems and products that process hundreds of billions of dollars in transaction volume annually for tens of millions of people.
So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Field Verification to join us in Spain.
About the role
Field Verification is how Moniepoint knows that the people and businesses on our platform are real. Every Moniepoint customer, retail and business, requires a completed field verification as part of KYC. The platform coordinates physical, in-person checks - verifying individuals, business owners, business addresses and loan guarantors - and it serves nearly every part of the company: onboarding, loans, compliance and the fraud team.
The system works today. A back office gives each business unit visibility and control over its own verification requests. A mobile-friendly web app puts the work in the hands of Field Verification Officers and the cluster leads who manage them across local government areas. An API layer lets other business units push verification requests in and receive results back by webhook, and an assignment algorithm routes each request to an officer close enough to carry it out.
We want to be straightforward about the rest. This domain has never had a dedicated engineering leader, and that is the single biggest constraint on it. The team is one lean, cross-functional squad - an Engineering Manager, four engineers and a QA - carrying verification volume for the entire customer base. They have done that impressively well, but running lean means running in keep-the-lights-on mode, and a long list of things that would make this platform substantially better has been waiting for someone to own it.
That list is the role. Trip and route management, so an officer can plan an optimal day across several sites rather than making a separate journey for each one - today we pay for a round trip per verification, and the logistics are nowhere near optimal. Capacity management. A native mobile app, wanted for a long time and never resourced. Liveness and identity verification tooling, exposed as APIs the rest of the business can build on. And as Moniepoint expands into markets where identity verification is as difficult as it is in Nigeria, Kenya among them, a platform that works beyond a single country.
There is a great deal of room to build here. Whoever takes this on will set the direction rather than inherit someone else's plan, on a system that already carries real weight for the business.

• Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Field Verification platform end to end, and setting direction for a domain that has been running without dedicated engineering leadership.

• Moving the platform from keep-the-lights-on operation to deliberate, prioritised development.

• Leading and growing the existing cross-functional team, and building the organisation out as scope expands.

• Building the operational efficiency layer - trip and route optimisation, task allocation and capacity management for field officers.

• Recruit, develop, empower, and engage a very hardworking team of Center Directors and teaching staff

• Drive consistent focus on quality, accreditation, and educational excellence throughout your district

• Nurture customer relationships throughout the market while driving and supporting sound business decisions with children and families in mind
